ROOT_CAUSE: A different vocabulary on each side of one comparison, plus a guard that disabled the only fallback in exactly the case it was written for. The grid row's occurrence key is the first and last date of its visible strip (ICEBOUND_TREASURE_TRAINING|10/02|10/06); the detail page prints its own dates (ICEBOUND_TREASURE_TRAINING|10/04|10/04). record_calendar_snapshot's EVENT_DETAIL branch matched on exact occurrence_key equality, and its single fallback was guarded by 'not occurrence' -- false whenever a key is present, i.e. in every case where the exact match can fail. So the 'already inspected' credit never landed, calendar_scan_pending stayed true, calendar_scan_due therefore stayed true, and the Brain -- which correctly asks 'is there an uninspected visible entry?' -- re-opened the same six entries for hours. Both keys are honest readings, so the defect is not a misread: the comparison was wrong. Corroboration: the other role completed its scan on the same grid because its last detail happened to yield a key equal to its row's, which is why this looked role-specific instead of general.

recommended_codex_review: Two invalid A/B attempts are worth recording as method, not detail: git stash push -- <path> silently no-ops on an already-committed file (prints 'No local changes to save'), and cmd.exe eats the ^ in 'git show <sha>^:path' under shell=True, so the comparison was against the same revision. Both produced a 'same failures on both sides' reading that proved nothing. Use explicit SHAs on this host.

core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means any git operation that touches a file rewrites the working copy as CRLF; md5 changes while git diff --numstat stays small (67/2 here). Worth an .gitattributes if byte-stable working files are ever needed for evidence hashing.
